hot.title: Is One Layer Enough? Training A Single Transformer Layer Can Match Full-Parameter RL Training
hot.summary: A study of large language model adaptation via reinforcement learning finds that performance gains are primarily concentrated in a stable subset of middle transformer layers, with single-layer training sometimes recovering over 100% of full-parameter training improvements and enabling more efficient training strategies.

hot.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
hot.summary: The "Program-as-Weights" (PAW) paradigm allows developers to define "fuzzy functions" using natural language, which are then compiled into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts. A Qwen3-0.6B interpreter running PAW programs achieved 73.78% exact match accuracy on the FuzzyBench dataset, outperforming a Qwen3-32B model (68.70%) while utilizing approximately 50 times less inference memory.

hot.title: A Mathematical Introduction to Diffusion Models
hot.summary: Jianfeng Lu's mathematical introduction to diffusion models unifies classical sampling dynamics with modern score-based generative processes, presenting a comprehensive, proof-oriented framework. It rigorously derives core concepts like reverse-time SDEs and probability flow ODEs, provides a detailed error analysis for diffusion samplers, and extends the theoretical understanding to discrete data and inference-time control.

hot.title: AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill
hot.summary: AUTOMEM introduces a framework enabling Large Language Models to automatically learn and optimize memory management as a cognitive skill, rather than a fixed architectural component. By iteratively refining memory structures and training a specialized memory component, the system significantly improves agent performance on long-horizon tasks, achieving 1.89x to 3.74x gains in progression rate and making open-weight models competitive with frontier proprietary systems.

hot.title: RoboDojo: A Unified Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Comprehensive Evaluation of Generalist Robot Manipulation Policies
hot.summary: RoboDojo introduces a unified sim-and-real benchmark for comprehensively evaluating generalist robot manipulation policies, featuring 42 simulation tasks and 18 reproducible real-world tasks across multiple robot embodiments. Initial evaluations of 30 policies on this platform reveal a substantial performance gap compared to human experts, particularly in generalization, precision, and open-semantic manipulation, alongside challenges in reliable real-world deployment.

hot.title: Vision Pretraining for Dense Spatial Perception
hot.summary: Robbyant researchers introduced masked boundary modeling, a self-supervised pretraining method for Vision Transformers that explicitly targets fine-grained spatial structure. The approach enabled a 1.1B parameter model to achieve an RMSE of 0.296 on NYU-Depth v2, surpassing larger models like the 7B DINOv3, and demonstrated leading performance in video object segmentation and depth completion.

hot.title: ResearchStudio-Idea: An Evidence-Grounded Research-Ideation Skill Suite from ML Conference Outcomes
hot.summary: ResearchStudio-Idea introduces an evidence-grounded skill suite, IdeaSpark, that extracts 15 operational ideation patterns from ML conference outcomes to guide large language models in generating high-quality research proposals. In an automated-judge study, IdeaSpark-generated ideas achieved a mean quality score of 3.87/4, ranking first in 88% of cases and maintaining competitive novelty compared to baseline LLMs.

hot.title: AdaJEPA: An Adaptive Latent World Model
hot.summary: AdaJEPA introduces an adaptive latent world model that continuously recalibrates its predictions during deployment, improving planning success for goal-conditioned control under visual and dynamics distribution shifts. This approach significantly boosts performance, such as doubling success rates on unseen object shapes, while incurring minimal computational overhead.

hot.title: EdgeBench: Unveiling Scaling Laws of Learning from Real-World Environments
hot.summary: A precise log-sigmoid scaling law governing the performance improvement of large language model agents from interaction in real-world environments was identified, exhibiting a mean R² of 0.998 on the new EdgeBench benchmark and revealing that frontier agent learning speed doubled every three months.

hot.title: Denser≠\neq=Better: Limits of On-Policy Self-Distillation for Continual Post-Training
hot.summary: On-policy self-distillation (SDPO) for continual LLM post-training offers strong in-domain specialization but exhibits increased forgetting and instability in sequential learning scenarios, a consequence of dense token-level supervision's sensitivity to teacher dynamics and artifact amplification, contrasting with more stable sequence-level reward methods.

hot.title: WorldDirector: Building Controllable World Simulators with Persistent Dynamic Memory
hot.summary: WorldDirector, a framework from HKUST and Ant Group, allows for building controllable video world simulators by explicitly decoupling semantic motion orchestration from visual generation. This approach ensures persistent dynamic object memory, maintaining consistent visual identity and physical logic for entities even after prolonged periods outside the camera's view, and facilitates unrestricted viewpoint exploration.

hot.title: UI-MOPD: Multi-Platform On-Policy Distillation for Continual GUI Agent Learning
hot.summary: Niu Lian et al. developed UI-MOPD, a multi-teacher on-policy distillation framework designed for continually learning GUI agents capable of operating across heterogeneous desktop and mobile platforms. The method achieved interactive task success rates of 38.2% on OSWorld and 12.0% on MobileWorld, outperforming baseline integration strategies and maintaining static GUI understanding and grounding capabilities.

hot.title: Orca: The World is in Your Mind
hot.summary: The Orca project by Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence proposes "Next-State-Prediction" as a unified paradigm for general world foundation models, learning a latent world representation from multimodal data through both unconscious and conscious learning. The model demonstrates scalable learning behavior and improved performance in text generation, physically plausible image prediction, and emergent action generation across diverse downstream tasks with a frozen backbone.

hot.title: VLA-Corrector: Lightweight Detect-and-Correct Inference for Adaptive Action Horizon
hot.summary: VLA-Corrector enhances the robustness of action-chunked Vision-Language-Action policies by introducing an inference-time framework that enables an adaptive action horizon and guided recovery. It improved average success rates by 15.65 percentage points on MetaWorld tasks for one VLA backbone and demonstrated a 17.7 percentage point increase in real-world robotic arm tasks, particularly in disturbance recovery.

hot.title: PointDiT: Pixel-Space Diffusion for Monocular Geometry Estimation
hot.summary: PointDiT introduces a minimalist pixel-space diffusion framework for estimating dense 3D point maps from single RGB images, bypassing the architectural complexities of latent diffusion models and intricate loss functions of deterministic regressors. The model sets new benchmarks in depth accuracy and boundary sharpness, achieving efficient single-step inference while providing sharper geometric details than prior approaches.

hot.title: PACE: A Proxy for Agentic Capability Evaluation
hot.summary: The PACE framework enables efficient and accurate prediction of large language model agent performance on costly agentic benchmarks by leveraging a small, automatically selected set of inexpensive non-agentic evaluation instances. This approach achieved an average LOOCV Mean Absolute Error of 3.80% for absolute performance prediction and 84.37% pairwise ranking accuracy, reducing evaluation costs by approximately 100 times compared to direct agentic evaluation.

hot.title: Learning to Move Before Learning to Do: Task-Agnostic pretraining for VLAs
hot.summary: A framework called Task-Agnostic Pretraining (TAP) teaches Vision-Language-Action models fundamental physical competence from abundant unlabeled data using inverse dynamics, then grounds these priors with minimal expert demonstrations. This approach achieved an average success rate of 33.32% on the SIMPLER benchmark, outperforming foundational models trained on limited expert data, and demonstrated enhanced robustness in real-world scenarios.

hot.title: DSpark: Confidence-Scheduled Speculative Decoding with Semi-Autoregressive Generation
hot.summary: A speculative decoding framework named DSpark integrates semi-autoregressive generation with confidence-scheduled verification to enhance Large Language Model inference efficiency. It significantly improves per-user generation speeds and aggregate throughput in live production environments by dynamically optimizing draft quality and resource allocation.

hot.title: Representation Distribution Matching for One-Step Visual Generation
hot.summary: Researchers systematically dissect Representation Distribution Matching (RDM) for one-step visual generation, identifying optimal design choices including a robust MMD estimation, large generated batch sizes, and a multi-encoder strategy with constrained optimization. The improved RDM (iRDM) achieves new state-of-the-art on ImageNet-256 for one-step generation and successfully post-trains FLUX.2 into a superior one-step text-to-image model, with its samples preferred over held-out real photographs in 63.6% of comparisons.

hot.title: Purified OPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation Without Losing How to Think
hot.summary: Researchers from Zhejiang University and Alibaba Group diagnosed that standard On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) fails in long Chain-of-Thought (long-CoT) models due to non-transferable supervision. They developed Purified OPSD (OPSD-PMI), which isolates and leverages only inference-transferable knowledge, leading to consistent performance improvements across various LLMs on mathematical reasoning tasks while preserving their reflective thinking capabilities.

The approach improves performance on semantic segmentation and as a frozen backbone for vision-language models, also demonstrating batch-size invariance.

likes.title: TRIAGE: Role-Typed Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: TRIAGE is a framework that refines credit assignment in agentic reinforcement learning by introducing a four-role semantic taxonomy and an LLM-based judge to provide segment-level process rewards, addressing the limitations of sparse, outcome-only feedback. The method consistently improved success rates across ALFWorld, Search-QA, and WebShop benchmarks by up to 18.4% and reduced rollout length in completed tasks by over 10%.

likes.title: ASPIRE: Agentic /Skills Discovery for Robotics
likes.summary: ASPIRE, a collaborative effort by researchers from NVIDIA, UMich, UIUC, UC Berkeley, and CMU, introduces a continual learning system for robotics that autonomously discovers, refines, and accumulates reusable skills. The framework significantly improves task success rates across various simulation benchmarks, facilitates zero-shot generalization to novel tasks, and demonstrates effective sim-to-real transfer by reducing real-world robot programming and debugging effort.

likes.title: Next-Generation Agentic Reinforcement Learning Systems Enable Self-Evolving Agents
likes.summary: Researchers from Ant Group, HKUST, and Tsinghua University introduce a comprehensive system architecture designed to enable self-evolving LLM agents at an enterprise scale. This architecture proposes a standardized data protocol, an enterprise-grade data proxy, and a unified evolution control plane, with a prototype implementation (AREAL2.0) demonstrating online policy LLM weight updates from deployed agent interactions.

likes.title: ABot-M0.5: Unified Mobility-and-Manipulation World Action Model
likes.summary: ABot-M0.5 unifies mobility and manipulation within a World Action Model by addressing structural misalignments in temporal granularity, action space, and train-test consistency. The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on mobile manipulation benchmarks and demonstrates effective transfer to real-world robotic systems with limited demonstrations.

likes.title: GR2 Technical Report
Xiaomi-GUI-0 Technical Report
likes.summary: Xiaomi-GUI-0, developed by the SeerRay Team, introduces an end-to-end multimodal GUI agent for real mobile environments, utilizing a real-device closed-loop training and evaluation paradigm. The 30-billion-parameter model achieves a 72.0% success rate on the new RealMobile benchmark and 78.9% on AndroidWorld, demonstrating robust performance in complex reasoning and planning.

likes.title: FARS: A Fully Automated Research System Deployed at Scale
likes.summary: FARS, a fully automated, end-to-end AI research system, was developed to continuously generate complete research papers from ideation to manuscript completion. During an initial deployment, the system produced 166 papers, with 11.4% of reviewed outputs receiving human ratings at or above a typical conference acceptance threshold, demonstrating scalable autonomous research capabilities while highlighting areas for improvement in scientific rigor.

likes.title: Measuring the Gap Between Human and LLM Research Ideas
likes.summary: Researchers at Yale and University of Chicago quantified the qualitative differences between research ideas generated by Large Language Models (LLMs) and human scientists, revealing that LLMs exhibit a significantly narrower "research taste". LLMs disproportionately generate "bridge-and-synthesis" ideas, showing a distinct pattern compared to the broader distribution of human-conceived research directions.

likes.title: Seed2.0 Model Card: Towards Intelligence Frontier for Real-World Complexity
likes.summary: Bytedance Seed introduces the Seed2.0 model series (Pro/Lite/Mini), designed to handle real-world complexity and optimize user experience in production environments. The models achieve competitive and often state-of-the-art performance across multimodal, language, and agentic tasks, including scientific coding and solving Olympiad-level math problems.

likes.title: QuasiMoTTo: Quasi-Monte Carlo Test-Time Scaling
likes.summary: QuasiMoTTo introduces a method for generating batches of correlated, yet marginally exact, samples from large language models, addressing inefficiencies in current i.i.d. sampling. This approach demonstrated a 25-47% reduction in required samples for test-time inference scaling across reasoning benchmarks and enabled policy-gradient reinforcement learning to reach target performance with 50% fewer training steps.

likes.title: Freeform Preference Learning for Robotic Manipulation
likes.summary: Freeform Preference Learning (FPL) enables robots to acquire nuanced behaviors by allowing humans to define and provide preferences along multiple natural-language axes, moving beyond ambiguous single binary choices. This method yielded policies that, on average, achieved a 38 percentage point higher success rate than baselines in real-world manipulation tasks and demonstrated compositional generalization and test-time steerability.
